caption: An extension cord is yanked out of the wall socket, and the lamp, radio and heater plugged into it all go off together.

sa.check: An extension cord in a wall socket with a lamp, a radio and a heater plugged into it.
The cord is yanked out of the socket.
The lamp, the radio and the heater all go off together.
All three are running before the yank: lamp lit, radio display lit, heater glowing or fan running.
The order is running, yank, all off.

pc.expect: All three devices go off at the moment the cord leaves the socket, and only then.
pc.fail: The cord is out and a device keeps running to the end of the clip; or a device goes off before the cord moves; or the devices go off one after another over the clip; or a device goes off with the cord still seated.

pc.expect: The three devices, the cord and the socket are the same before and after: the same items in the same places, dark rather than gone.
pc.fail: A device vanishes rather than switching off; or a fourth device appears; or a device changes place; or the cord splits into two cords.

pc.expect: Once the cord is out the devices stay off; the heater's glow, if any, only fades and does not return.
pc.fail: A device comes back on with the cord out; or the lamp flickers; or the heater's glow brightens after the yank; or the cord jumps back into the socket.

pc.expect: The cord is drawn taut by the yank and goes slack once the plug is free; it stays attached at both ends.
pc.fail: The cord stretches like elastic; or stands rigid in the air after the plug is out; or the cord floats; or the devices are dragged across the floor by the yank.

pc.expect: The plug leaves the socket whole; nothing passes through the wall; the devices keep their shape.
pc.fail: The plug passes through the wall beside the socket; or the cord passes through a device; or a device changes shape; or the socket comes off the wall.

pc.expect: Everything in view, named in the caption or not, keeps its number, identity and shape unless something visible acts on it, and nothing passes through anything else.
pc.fail: An object that nothing visible acts on appears from nothing; or vanishes while still in frame and not occluded; or duplicates or merges with another; or turns into a different object or a different shape between frames; or any object passes through another. Changes brought about by the caption's event or by a visible interaction, objects leaving the frame, and occlusion are not failures.

pc.expect: The devices' colours, the cord's colour and the room stay the same apart from the lights.
pc.fail: A device changes colour; or the cord changes colour; or the room's contents rearrange.

note: The radio falling silent is sound and is not judged; the radio counts through its display or dial light.
